newsitem.title: UK: Stg/mark slices through 3.05, tracks dlr/mark.
newsitem.headline: Stg/mark slices through 3.05, tracks dlr/mark.

text.p: The pound motored higher and through 3.05 marks in Europe, borne along by a strong dollar/mark and June industrial output figures, traders said.
They said an increasingly likely base rate rise after a two-day Bank of England Monetary policy committee beginning on Wdnesday was also supporting sterling.
" It's (sterling/mark) has been capped there (3.05) for the last two days but now the pressure looks great," said Lee Ferridge, currency strategist at Commerzbank.
At 0945 GMT, sterling stood at 3.0540/50 marks and up over 1-1/2 pfennings from 3.0363 marks in late Europe on Monday.
Tony Norfield, treasury economist at ABN Amro, however, said sterling/mark's push higher was likely to stall short of July 23 peaks around 3.0878 marks - its highest level since August 1989.
Analysts said figures for British June industrial output, up 1.4 percent month-on-month and 1.9 percent year-on-year, while not striking, were enough to give the pound an added fillip.
"Technically, there's no reason why it shouldn't hit 3.08 but it'll be restrained by a number of factors," Norfield said.
Economists said interest rates were beginning to show signs of affecting the services industry, unaffected so far by a powering sterling which has stifled exports.
"The pound is significantly overblown," but it's a scary game, telling when the turn might come," Norfield said.
Some traders expressed surprise that the Labour government, in office since May, had taken no measures to attempt to curb sterling and soften any forthcoming fall.
"It's as if they were sleeping for the moment," one said. -- Ralph Boulton, London newsroom +44 171-542 89 68
